qa.title: Q2235 (Aug. 7, 2026)
qa.question: I have a Shion, Immortal Aegis on the field with "For the rest of this turn, if it would take damage, it takes that much +2 instead." How much damage does it take if it is attacked by a 1-attack enemy follower?
qa.answer:
It would take either 0 damage or 2 damage, depending on your decision.

When there are multiple abilities modifying damage dealt, the player who controls the follower receiving the damage decides the order in which the abilities are applied. In this case, depending on the order, the final damage taken can be calculated either of the following two ways:

1. Shion, Immortal Aegis takes 0 damage because you decide to apply its ability first, reducing 1 damage to 0. Then, since taking 0 damage doesn't count as taking damage at all, there is no instance of damage that would be modified by +2.

2. Shion, Immortal Aegis takes 2 damage because you decide to apply the +2 damage first, modifying the damage taken to 3, which is then reduced to 2 by Shion, Immortal Aegis's ability.

qa.title: Q2265 (Aug. 7, 2026)
qa.question: Can you explain "Your opponents must select this for abilities if able" in detail?
qa.answer:
According to the Comprehensive Rules, "if multiple effects that require a player to perform a certain action are produced simultaneously, and it is not possible to perform all of them, the player is required to select and perform as many of the actions as possible."

Let's look at some examples of this in action. In the following, X denotes a follower with "Whenever an opponent is selecting cards for an ability, if they can select this card, they must select it," and Y denotes a follower that doesn't have this ability.

Example 1: Your field has 1 X and 2 Y. An opponent is selecting "up to 1" follower for an ability. In this case, they must select the X.

Example 2: Your field has 2 X and 2 Y. An opponent is selecting "up to 1" follower for an ability. In this case, they must select one of the two X's.

Example 3: Your field has 1 X and 2 Y. An opponent is selecting "up to 2" followers for an ability. In this case, they must select the X, but whether or not they select a Y is up to them.

Example 4: Your field has 2 X and 2 Y. An opponent is selecting "up to 2" followers for an ability. In this case, they must select both X's.

Example 5: Your field has 3 X and 2 Y. An opponent is selecting "up to 2" followers for an ability. In this case, they must select two of the three X's.

qa.title: Q2264 (Aug. 7, 2026)
qa.question: What does "Your opponents must select this for abilities if able" mean?
qa.answer:
It means that when an opponent is playing an ability that requires them to "select" one or more cards, such as "Select an enemy follower on the field and deal it 2 damage," if they are able to select this follower, then they must select it.

Note that this ability is only valid when this follower on the field. Also, when an opponent is attacking with a follower, they don't have to select this follower as the attack target.

qa.title: Q2263 (Aug. 7, 2026)
qa.question: If this follower is given Aura, do opponents still have to select it for abilities?
qa.answer: No. Aura would prevent them from selecting it.
